To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

funders of health research have a number of reasons for encouraging and supporting the involvement of consumers in health-related research, and that they do so in a variety of ways, but they are not always clear about the parameters of acceptableness.

'Many UK funders are promoting consumer involvement in their funded research. They have several reasons for this and are using various ways to encourage and support researchers in involving consumers.'

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
consumer involvement is an important aspect of research and funders should encourage it.
the UK research funders have a commitment to consumer involvement in health-related research and have taken a number of steps to promote this.
consumer involvement is a desirable and important part of research, but it is not a prerequisite for funding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the consumer involvement agenda is being taken seriously by funders, but that there is still a way to go before the full potential of consumer involvement in health-related research is realized.
consumer involvement is not just a 'good idea' but is also a 'good business practice' that is becoming an integral part of the research process.
funders should be more transparent about their policies on consumer involvement and the ways they encourage it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for funders of research to work more closely with consumer groups and with research users to develop more effective ways of supporting and promoting consumer involvement.
funders should be aware of how consumer involvement is defined and measured, and that they should be clear about the criteria for funding consumer-involvement projects.
